pr_title: Allow interop resolvers to return self handle
pr_body:
When user-defined resolvers return self handle via `GetMainProgramHandle()`, we lookup the cached handle in mono and fail to find one because `internal_module` is not cached in `native_library_module_map`.

Fix is to test the resolver returned handle against self; before the map lookup (which happens under the lock).

Close #77985.

issue_context.title: Handle returned GetMainProgramHandle() not sufficient for resolving statically linked native symbols on iOS
issue_context.body:
### Description

Based on the discussion in #57610 we were under the impression that using `GetMainProgramHandle()` in tandem with `NativeLibrary.SetDllImportResolver()` would be a replacement for having to modify third party packages to use `[DllImport("_Internal")]` on iOS. So far in testing on .NET 7 this has not been the case. 

I created a sample native iOS library (libsayhello) and a wrapping C# lib which handles [DllImport("libsayhello')]. Then within a sample Maui app I added Interop code to allow my lib to be statically linked into the main application at compile time, then attempted to catch the resolution of 'libsayhello' in the import resolver and return the handle returned by GetMainProgramHandle(). 








### Reproduction Steps

A test app showing the behavior is located at [stanger/ResolverTest](https://github.com/stanger/ResolverTest).

### Expected behavior

DllImport calls for 'libsayhello' should be able to resolved to their statically linked symbols in the main binary.

### Actual behavior

DllNotFoundException

### Regression?

_No response_

### Known Workarounds

_No response_

### Configuration

.NET: 7.0.100-rc.2.22477.23
iOS 16 and MacOS 13 (originally discovered on iOS)
Tested on x64 and ARM64

### Other information

_No response_

I see the problem. We definitely should have caught this earlier as this was the end-to-end scenario...

Sometimes, the value returned by `GetMainProgramHandle()` is `IntPtr.Zero`, as that's the handle to use for this case. However, `SetDllImportResolver` expects the delegate to return `IntPtr.Zero` for the failure case. As a result, using `GetMainProgramHandle` with `SetDllImportResolver` as it exists today has a fundamental problem on platforms where `IntPtr.Zero` is the correct handle for this case.

I see a few solutions here:

1. Introduce an API specifically for resolving `DllImport`s to the main program handle (what we were trying to avoid).
2. Introduce an overload of `SetDllImportResolver` that takes a delegate that returns `IntPtr?` instead of `IntPtr`. The user experience here would be pretty rough though as overload resolution would prefer the `IntPtr` overload for target-typed lambdas unless we got something like https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/65965 (I don't think ref-assembly tricks would work here well).

> Sometimes, the value returned by `GetMainProgramHandle()` is `IntPtr.Zero`

Going by: 
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/02c3e95fc2f87dcabfea8bef2c1b1a48c2249d9d/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Runtime/InteropServices/NativeLibrary.cs#L261 it throws an exception instead of returning `IntPtr.Zero`.

In which case, I'm not sure what would be causing a `DllNotFoundException` specifically.

@stranger, can you confirm what `GetMainProgramHandle` is returning?
This is the value I see in the debugger is: `handle 0xfffffffffffffffe`

Hmm. In that case, I'm not sure the issue off the top of my head.

Can you get the stack trace for where the exception is thrown from? I don't have a Mac handy at the moment.

Also, can you try adding `__attribute__((visibility(default)))` to the native definition of your `say_hello` method?

The stack trace isn't overly verbose and the inner exception was null.

`System.DllNotFoundException: libsayhello
   at ResolverSample.MainPage.OnCounterClicked(Object sender, EventArgs e) in /Users/stanger/Workspaces/Enclave/ResolverSample/src/ResolverSample/MainPage.xaml.cs:line 17`

I have also updated the sample lib definition with `__attribute__((visibility("default")))`

Why do we free `s_handle` here? That seems like we're asking for trouble.  `free (IntPtr.Zero)` would also work (`free (NULL)` is a no-op call - so we would just test that the we got the right symbol, which is what we want).

I'm assuming the failure on the mono interpreter legs is somehow related (we need to keep the native handle around longer for some reason?)

The reason why it is working everywhere is we bail out for internal handle: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/83c61ae6b6be3b43f91d4c5bd63a1f3e93145c1a/src/mono/mono/metadata/native-library.c#L1250 (same in coreclr) and I saw another test doing the same. IL interpreter has another issue with this code that it fails like this:

> Test Failure: System.InvalidProgramException: Invalid IL code in (wrapper managed-to-native) MainProgramHandleTests:free (void*): IL_0012: calli     0x00000003

it is a valid IL, so the bug is in the interpreter itself.
I'm trying with `getppid()`. Seems like it will work everywhere (test on osx-arm64 and android-arm64). Lets try that after this CI run completes.
Nvm, it didn't help. IL interp needs to be fixed. :)
